record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Can a weak Cauchy surface, defined as a pointwise limit of Cauchy surfaces, in a globally hyperbolic spacetime satisfying suitable energy conditions contain an inextendible null geodesic?

evidence.quote: Show that a weak Cauchy surface (i.e. a pointwise limit of a sequence of Cauchy surfaces) in a globally hyperbolic spacetime satisfying suitable energy conditions, cannot contain an inextendible null geodesic.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a globally hyperbolic spacetime (i.e., a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian manifold that admits a Cauchy surface, equivalently is strongly causal and has compact causal diamonds $J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$). Recall that a Cauchy surface is an achronal subset of $M$ that is met exactly once by every inextendible timelike curve. Call a subset $S\subset M$ a weak Cauchy surface if there exists a sequence $\{S_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of Cauchy surfaces in $M$ such that $S$ is the pointwise limit of $\{S_n\}$ (that is, $S$ consists of all points $p\in M$ for which there exist $p_n\in S_n$ with $p_n\to p$, in a manner making $S$ the pointwise limit of the $S_n$). Assume $(M,g)$ satisfies suitable energy conditions (for instance the null energy condition $\mathrm{Ric}(k,k)\geq 0$ for all null vectors $k$).

Question: Can such a weak Cauchy surface $S$ contain an inextendible null geodesic of $(M,g)$? Equivalently, prove or disprove: under these hypotheses, no weak Cauchy surface in $(M,g)$ contains an inextendible null geodesic.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not yield a published resolution of this specific question about weak Cauchy surfaces (pointwise limits of Cauchy surfaces) containing inextendible null geodesics. Related work on null geometry and Cauchy horizons by Galloway, and recent results on global hyperbolicity via null distance (Burtscher–García-Heveling), touch on adjacent themes but do not appear to settle the stated problem. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Null Geometry and the Einstein Equations (Galloway)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses null hypersurfaces, achronal boundaries ruled by null geodesics, and rigidity results in globally hyperbolic spacetimes.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related rigidity results exist but do not directly resolve the weak Cauchy surface problem.

status_evidence.title: Global Hyperbolicity through the Eyes of the Null Distance
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes global hyperbolicity via completeness in the null distance of weak temporal functions and properties of their level sets.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on causal/Cauchy-type level sets does not appear to settle the question.
